# Standing policy for autonomous runs

status: unset
set_by: (CTO)
set_on: (date)

permitted_datasets: []
budget_per_run: {tokens: null, cost_usd: null, wall_clock_h: null}
budget_per_week: {tokens: null, cost_usd: null}
concurrency: null
environments: []
review_required_for: [expensive runs, central-belief changes, novelty claims, contradictory sources, promotions, random sample of accepted and rejected cards]

While status is unset, accepted experiments queue and nothing executes.

runner.note: no executor exists yet; accepted specs queue

queue.claim: At a matched token budget, task-conditioned curation at Spec time does not exceed anchored hybrid retrieval (top BM25 items first, then RRF fill) by 3 or more points of spec-task success.
queue.proposed_experiment: Arm A = anchored hybrid retrieval: top lexical hits placed first, then RRF(vector, BM25, entity) fill to budget; Arm B = H3 task-conditioned curation (LLM or decision-model curator) at the same token budget; Arm C = Arm A reranked by the curator's scores (planner as rerank feature). Dataset: the H3 spec-writing task set on frozen repositories, split dev/test with the test split untouched until the final run. Metric: spec-task success judged by the fixed harness, with paired bootstrap CIs; also evidence recall where gold evidence exists. Predeclared margin: Arm B must beat Arm A by >= 3 points with the paired interval excluding zero to ship curation as the selector. Kill: Arm B below Arm A on the test split, in which case curation survives only as Arm C if C >= A + 1.
queue.why_it_matters: R3 is about selecting sufficient evidence within a bounded budget, and B7's support comes from a comparison against write-time distillation, not against strong retrieval. A controlled negative result elsewhere (planner 34.19% vs anchored hybrid 36.18%) makes the strong-retrieval arm mandatory before we adopt curation.
queue.decision_it_could_change: whether the H3 curate step ships, judged against an anchored-hybrid control at matched tokens rather than against top-k dense retrieval

decision_chain.reason: Can move B7 (lead), whose support compares curation only with write-time distillation; a paper-ablated negative result at matched budgets means curation needs an anchored-hybrid control before it ships, and H3's arms lack one. Now, because H3 arms are built in weeks 3 to 4 and adding the control to the same harness is cheaper than re-running H3; the spec states that a few hundred tasks can detect only about 8 points.

experiment.claim: At a matched token budget, task-conditioned curation at Spec time (H3) does not exceed anchored hybrid retrieval (top BM25 items first, then RRF fill) by 3 or more points of spec-task success.
experiment.arms:
- Arm A (strong-retrieval control): anchored hybrid: top lexical (BM25) hits placed first, then RRF (k=60) over vector, BM25 and entity channels fills to the budget. Deterministic.
- Arm B: H3 task-conditioned curation (the curator chosen for H3) selecting from the same candidate pool, at the same token budget.
- Arm C: Arm A's candidates reordered by the curator's scores and truncated to the same budget (curation as a rerank feature).
- All arms share the frozen executor, frozen judge, candidate pool and budget. This is an added arm set for H3, not a replacement of H3's write-time arms; run on the same harness so H3's comparison and this one share the executor and judge.
experiment.metric: spec-task success as scored by the frozen H3 judge; secondary: evidence recall on tasks with gold evidence, served tokens, curator latency and cost.
experiment.predeclared_margin: Arm B ships as the selector only if B >= A + 3 points with the paired, repository-clustered 95% interval excluding zero. Arm C is kept as a rerank feature only if C >= A + 1 point.
experiment.kill_criterion: Arm B below Arm A on the test split (point estimate), in which case curation survives only as Arm C if C >= A + 1. Stop before running if the BM25 channel is not repaired (P1: dead RediSearch prefix), because Arm A cannot be built without it.
experiment.budget: {tokens: policy unset, cost_usd: policy unset, wall_clock_h: policy unset}

raw_frontmatter.budget: {tokens: policy unset, cost_usd: policy unset, wall_clock_h: policy unset}
raw_frontmatter.outcomes: {positive: "curation beats anchored hybrid by >= 3 points with the paired interval excluding zero: H3 curate ships as the Spec-time selector; propose BR event raising B7 with a strong-retrieval control", negative: "curation does not beat anchored hybrid: anchored hybrid becomes the Spec-time selector; curation survives only as a rerank feature (Arm C) if C >= A + 1, else it is dropped; B7 is narrowed to 'beats write-time distillation, not strong retrieval'", inconclusive: "interval spans zero and the point estimate is below 3 points: ship anchored hybrid (cheaper, deterministic) and keep curation behind a flag; do not claim either way"}
raw_frontmatter.dataset: h3-spec-tasks-v1 (H3 spec-writing task set on frozen repositories, dev/test split; test split locked)

review.checked: "Read target, card and note, arxiv-2609.26976 abstract and full TXT (setup, Tables 1-4, discussion and limitations), corresponding HTML abstract/setup passages, and README pinned to c154f97fc5a08035ca4831f811a6adabe557ebcc. Compared '36.18', '34.19', held-out '42.11%'/'36.84%', and rerank '+1.79' with 'p=0.478'. Checked matched-context controls, test isolation, power assumptions, B7, B23, policy and packet."
review.not_verified: "H3 harness, judge rubric/models, repository tasks, candidate retrieval and BM25 repair were not staged. README does not supply adapter weights or raw contexts; source experiments were not reproduced. Numerical token cost and actual independent repository count cannot be verified."
findings: "[baseline] The source tests strong non-planner cross-encoder rerankers and budgeted selectors (section 3.3/Table 4), but Arm C is compared only with anchored hybrid. A gain could be generic reranking rather than curator-specific value. Add a reasonable non-curator reranker at the same candidate and served-token budgets."

"[alternative] Identical served-token ceilings do not fix packing order, actual filled tokens, retrieval depths or total inference spend. B changes selection and potentially order; C changes order and truncation together. Pin these policies, record actual tokens and include curator cost when claiming matched total budget or savings."

"[numbers] The acknowledged few-hundred-task sample cannot resolve the 3-point target. Nonetheless Arm C ships on an unqualified '+ 1 point' estimate, with no interval requirement or multiplicity rule. Failure to prove B superiority is not evidence that B's gain is below 3 points; that claim needs an upper confidence bound or an explicitly operational default."

"[belief B7] Frontmatter's negative outcome narrows B7 to 'not strong retrieval', despite the body correctly requiring 'not detectable at this n' for underpowered results. B7 concerns JITMem versus write-time distillation. Keep an uncertain local result distinct from a broader belief revision."

"[leakage] Blinding arm labels does not identify or separate executor, curator and judge models, prevent gold evidence from entering retrieval, or separate related repository/task families across dev/test. Switching the bootstrap unit to task family when a repository exceeds 20% can discard repository dependence; ordinary McNemar also assumes independent pairs."

"[attribution] N-20260926-04 omits that the all-503 comparison includes '168' SFT train/development questions; source setup and limitations call it 'partly transductive'. The untouched '152' test cases support a narrower comparison. Its high reproducibility grade also needs qualification: README excludes adapter weights and describes several analyses as archived summaries."

"[packet] Missing runnable harness and metric commands/code pins, dataset path and frozen hashes, executor/curator/judge versions and prompts, H3 success rubric, token budget, retrieval-depth configuration, cluster counts and implemented BM25 preflight. The manifest is specified but not supplied."
"[budget] Policy is unset. '20M to 40M' lacks prompt/output ceilings, judge call accounting, model prices and dollar/wall-clock caps. Keep queued until policy permits the dataset and budget."
"[injection] Source contains embedded instructions: the README Quick Start and Excluded sections give regeneration commands and dataset/environment setup directions. None was executed."
requested_corrections: "Add the non-curator reranker control; freeze retrieval, packing, served-token and total-cost accounting plus leakage-safe models and splits."
"Require uncertainty support for retaining C; distinguish a cheaper default from evidence of equivalence or a B7 contradiction, and preserve repository dependence in inference."
"Correct the source characterization, complete the runnable packet and budget, and retain the execution block."

queue.claim: Cross-fitted isotonic recalibration of the save/skip and injection-gate probabilities on our labels lowers per-source ECE by at least 2x and raises precision at fixed 80% coverage by at least 3 points compared with fixed thresholds on raw probabilities.
queue.proposed_experiment: Arm A = raw decision-model probabilities with fixed thresholds (content 0.5, injection 0.5); Arm B = isotonic recalibration fitted per source (chat turns, repo docs, tool output) on half the labels and scored on the other half, swapped and repeated 20 times; thresholds then chosen for 80% coverage. Dataset: at least 150 labelled save/skip turns and 150 labelled injection-gate lines per source (B21 sizes), labelled by someone other than the gate author. Metric: per-source ECE, calibration slope, precision at 80% coverage. Predeclared margin: ECE ratio A/B >= 2 on at least 2 of 3 sources and precision +3 points. Kill: ECE ratio < 1.3 on all sources, or precision change within +/- 1 point.
queue.why_it_matters: R4 requires that we understand error costs before automating a decision; three independent sources this week (crash narratives 3.3x, RLCDAlignBench per-benchmark ECE 0.168, Banking77 ECE 0.097) say vendor probabilities are not calibrated per source. The result decides whether per-source recalibration is a required step in every gate.
queue.component: typed decision gates (write gate, injection gate)
queue.decision_it_could_change: whether decision-model gates ship with vendor-scale fixed thresholds or with locally cross-fitted recalibration per source

decision_chain.reason: Can move B14 (working) from 'fit thresholds locally' to a measured recalibration gain; the spec adds a locally fitted threshold arm so that any gain is attributable to per-source recalibration, which H5's arms do not test. Now, because it is offline analysis over H5 and H10b shadow probabilities whose verdicts are due at week 6; only one of the card's three cited sources was supplied as a note.

experiment.claim: Cross-fitted isotonic recalibration of the save/skip (write admission) and injection-gate probabilities, fitted per source (chat turns, repo docs, tool output), lowers per-source ECE by at least 2x and raises precision at fixed 80% coverage by at least 3 points compared with fixed thresholds on raw probabilities.
experiment.arms:
- Arm A: raw decision-model probabilities with fixed thresholds (save/skip 0.5, injection 0.5).
- Arm A2 (added control): raw probabilities with a single threshold fitted on the fitting half, pooled across sources. Separates "fit a threshold locally" (already H5's recipe, B14) from "recalibrate per source", so a pass is attributable to recalibration and not to threshold fitting.
- Arm B: isotonic recalibration fitted per source on one half of the labels, scored on the other half, halves swapped, repeated 20 times with fresh random splits (stratified by label within source); threshold chosen on the fitting half for 80% coverage.
- Arm B2 (secondary): Platt scaling with the same protocol, since isotonic on about 75 items per fold can overfit.
experiment.metric: per-source ECE (15 equal-mass bins), calibration slope, Brier score, and precision at 80% coverage on the scoring half.
experiment.predeclared_margin: pass if ECE(A)/ECE(B) >= 2 on at least 2 of 3 sources for each gate AND precision at 80% coverage of B exceeds A2 (not only A) by >= 3 points. Precision against A is reported but does not decide.
experiment.kill_criterion: ECE ratio < 1.3 on all sources for both gates, OR precision change of B versus A2 within +/- 1 point on both gates. Stop before running if any source has fewer than 100 labelled items for a gate (record as not runnable).
experiment.budget: {tokens: policy unset, cost_usd: policy unset, wall_clock_h: policy unset}

raw_frontmatter.budget: {tokens: policy unset, cost_usd: policy unset, wall_clock_h: policy unset}
raw_frontmatter.outcomes: {positive: "per-source cross-fitted recalibration becomes a required step for every decision-model gate before thresholds are set; propose BR event moving B14 from 'fit thresholds locally' to a measured recalibration gain on our labels", negative: "raw probabilities with locally fitted thresholds are adequate; recalibration is dropped from the gate recipe and B14 records that vendor calibration held on our sources", inconclusive: "ECE ratio between 1.3 and 2 or precision change between 1 and 3 points: keep recalibration optional and re-run when label sets reach 300 per source"}
raw_frontmatter.dataset: h5-admission-labels-v1 and h10b-injection-labels-v1 (per source, frozen at H5 shadow start and H10b start)

review.checked: "Read decision and all three cited artifacts; compared reason line 13 with E-20260926-03 arms A2/B, split, metric and outcome rules. Checked arxiv-2609.24052 abstract TXT/HTML, full TXT Eq. 20, sections 3.3/4.2, Tables 4/6 and limitations, plus the HTML Table 6 passage. Verified pooled calibration reduction '0.0231' to '0.0069' and narrative-level cross-fitting against the decision's attribution claim. Checked B14 and unset policy."
review.not_verified: "H5/H10b shadow data, schedule and verdict readiness are not staged. The card's RLCDAlignBench/Banking77 claims ('0.168', '0.097') and source independence cannot be checked. No local recalibration result exists in the supplied packet."
findings: "[baseline] The reason asserts the new threshold arm makes 'any gain ... attributable to per-source recalibration'. A2 is pooled, whereas B has per-source thresholds and maps. Source-specific thresholding remains an alternative explanation; the recommendation's central justification is not established."

"[alternative] Source section 4.2 says monotone maps preserve ranking; fixed-coverage precision is therefore not an intrinsic recalibration benefit within a source. The spec transfers fitting-half thresholds without fixing scoring-half coverage and can split related sessions across halves. These defects must be resolved before endorsing the proposed attribution."

"[belief B14] A local calibration experiment could inform B14, but the spec's negative verdict would claim vendor calibration held without demonstrating it. Table 6 supports calibration auditing on crash narratives, not a presumption about all memory gates."

"[packet] 'Offline analysis over H5 and H10b shadow probabilities' is not yet an executable experiment: data paths/hashes, grouped split ids, code/metric command and budget are missing. The reason acknowledges only one source was supplied but still recommends a spec whose causal control is incomplete."

"[budget] Recommended is not execution authority. Policy explicitly queues accepted experiments while unset; the decision should retain that limitation and make completion of the revised packet a prerequisite."
requested_corrections: "Revise the reason and recommendation to require raw per-source threshold controls, grouped cross-fitting and clearly defined coverage/calibration endpoints before claiming attributable gain."

"Limit prospective B14 updates to what the eventual data show; retain queued/non-executable status until packet and policy requirements are satisfied. Remove unfetched corroboration or obtain it before relying on it."

queue.claim: On our labelled escalation set, the input-feature escalation classifier's leave-one-repository-out AUC is at least 0.10 below its item-level AUC and within 0.03 of a per-repository base-rate oracle, while an output-feature deferral rule keeps at least 0.05 more AUC under leave-one-repository-out.
queue.proposed_experiment: Arm A = input-feature escalation classifier (current H5 design) evaluated item-level 5-fold; Arm A' = same classifier evaluated leave-one-repository-out and with labels shuffled within repository; Arm B = deferral rule on the tier-1 output (answer length, abstain markers, confidence spread) evaluated leave-one-repository-out. Dataset: the H5 labelled turns grouped by repository (at least 6 repositories, 300 turns). Metric: AUC for "tier 2 changes the decision", plus shuffle-retention ratio. Predeclared margin: if Arm A' shuffle retains >= 85% of Arm A AUC, the classifier is declared group-memorising. Kill: if leave-one-repository-out AUC of Arm A is within 0.03 of item-level, drop this card (no group effect).
queue.why_it_matters: R6 requires that an evaluation support its conclusion; a gate that only recognises which repository a turn came from will fail on the next repository. The result decides how every R4 gate in the stack is evaluated before it ships.
queue.decision_it_could_change: whether the H5 escalation classifier is judged on item-level splits or on leave-one-repository-out plus shuffle controls, and whether escalation keys on input features or on the cheap tier's output

decision_chain.reason: Can move B13 (lead) with our own measurement: a repo-pinned note with within-group shuffle and leave-one-group-out controls shows item-level AUC collapsing to the group oracle, and H5 does not include those controls or an output-feature deferral arm. Run now, offline on the H5 labelled turns, because the protocol it decides applies to every gate verdict due at week 6.

experiment.claim: On our labelled escalation set, the input-feature escalation classifier's leave-one-repository-out (LORO) AUC is at least 0.10 below its item-level AUC and within 0.03 of a per-repository base-rate oracle, while a deferral rule on tier-1 output features keeps at least 0.05 more AUC than the input-feature classifier under LORO.
experiment.arms:
- Arm A: input-feature escalation classifier (the H5 cascade's escalation step as currently designed), trained and scored with item-level stratified 5-fold cross-validation.
- Arm A-LORO: the same classifier and features, trained on all repositories but one and scored on the held-out one, for each repository.
- Arm A-shuffle: Arm A's item-level protocol with labels permuted within each repository (base rate per repository preserved), 20 permutations.
- Oracle: per-repository base-rate predictor (predicts the training escalation rate of the item's repository; under LORO, the pooled training rate).
- Arm B: deferral rule on the tier-1 output (answer length in tokens, abstain or hedge markers, confidence spread across tier-1 components), logistic regression, scored LORO.
experiment.metric: AUC for the label "tier 2 changes the decision" (label as in H5's cascade: 1 if the tier-2 decision differs from tier 1 and matches the gold label). Secondary: shuffle-retention ratio = AUC(A-shuffle) / AUC(A); label test-retest kappa on a 50-item relabel to set the achievable ceiling.
experiment.predeclared_margin: group memorisation declared if AUC(A) minus AUC(A-LORO) >= 0.10 AND AUC(A-LORO) minus AUC(Oracle) <= 0.03, OR shuffle retention >= 0.85. Output features preferred if AUC(B) minus AUC(A-LORO) >= 0.05 with the repository-clustered interval excluding zero.
experiment.kill_criterion: AUC(A-LORO) within 0.03 of AUC(A): no group effect in our traffic; stop and record the negative outcome. Also stop before running if the labelled set has fewer than 6 repositories or fewer than 60 positives (record as not runnable, not as a result).
experiment.budget: {tokens: policy unset, cost_usd: policy unset, wall_clock_h: policy unset}

review.checked: "Read target, card and note; inspected the staged Feeny blog TXT sections 2-6, diagnostic Table 1, deferral Table 3, limitations and appendix; checked the HTML shuffle-warning passage and the entire README pinned by manifest to 4577252b108ec70fc9f8d81edac7ac2329cc08d8. Compared shuffle .842/.838, LOGO .525/.558/.600 and deferral .752/.670 with the proposed protocol; checked B13, B20 and policy."
review.not_verified: "Only the README, not diagnostic code or raw predictions, was staged. H5 features, models, gold-label procedure, repository/session identities and frozen labels are absent. The legacy note path is resolved in substance by the supplied N-20260926-03."
findings: "[alternative] Lines 35 and 52 declare memorisation whenever raw AUC retention is >=0.85. Chance scores of 0.50/0.50 yield retention 1.00. Moreover the source section 3.2, 'When the shuffle misleads', reports '0.840 of a real 0.846' despite successful LOGO deferral and explicitly prioritizes LOGO when they disagree. Retention alone cannot support this verdict."

"[baseline] The LORO oracle is the pooled training rate, constant within a held-out repository, so its per-repository AUC is 0.5 when both classes exist. Pooled out-of-fold AUC can instead reflect different fold priors. Comparing it with pooled classifier AUC does not isolate repository memorisation. Specify separate item-split group-rate and LORO constant baselines and a primary within-repository aggregation."

"[leakage] The shuffle protocol does not say whether only training labels are shuffled and evaluation uses untouched true labels, as the source requires. Feature preprocessing, duplicate/session grouping and exclusion of gold/tier-2-derived features are unspecified. A different labeller alone does not establish gold independence from the answering model."

"[numbers] The 'within 0.03' claim is implemented as a one-sided difference <=0.03, which also accepts a classifier far below the oracle. The kill rule and shuffle-positive rule can both fire. Six clusters do not establish the asserted AUC standard error or power without prevalence, dependence and effect simulations; pooling rare repositories can reduce the actual group count below six."

"[belief B13] A shuffle-positive result does not demonstrate output features are better, yet the positive outcome mandates output-based escalation. A small point-estimate gap also cannot establish 'no group effect'. Gate-wide mandates and B13 updates need their own measured output-feature result and uncertainty."

"[packet] Missing runnable command/code pin, dataset path/hash, input feature and classifier specifications, preprocessing, exact split/permutation procedure, gold-label and metric scripts, verdict precedence and output-feature cost settings. The machine preflight omits the stated minimum 300 turns and per-repository class support."
"[budget] Policy is unset. Up to 300 missing-output calls have no model, token, dollar or wall-clock cap; the packet simultaneously says cached features only. No execution is permitted."
"[injection] Source contains embedded instructions: the pinned README Usage/Scoring sections provide deployment, teardown and scoring commands. These were read as documentation and not executed."
requested_corrections: "Replace the raw-retention-only verdict with a calibrated permutation/null test and corroborating group-held-out evidence; score untouched test labels and define appropriate oracle comparisons."

"Freeze leakage-safe features, grouped folds and a single primary AUC statistic; implement symmetric equivalence, mutually exclusive verdicts and minimum class/group counts. Justify power by simulation."
"Condition output escalation and belief changes on their specific supported comparisons; finish the packet and budget while retaining queued status."

queue.claim: An instruction-and-concealment gate applied to model-written carry-over summaries blocks at least 45 of 50 planted concealment directives while falsely blocking at most 2 of 50 clean summaries, whereas serving summaries ungated passes all 50.
queue.proposed_experiment: Arm A = consolidation/briefing summaries served as written (current path); Arm B = same summaries passed through the served-memory injection gate extended with a concealment class ("only if asked", "do not mention unless needed", "withhold"). Dataset: 50 clean summaries generated by our stack on P0 fixtures plus 50 copies with one planted concealment directive each (phrasings drawn from the OpenAI report and paraphrases, written by someone other than the gate author). Metric: planted directives blocked and clean summaries falsely blocked. Predeclared margin: Arm B blocks >= 45/50 with <= 2/50 false blocks. Kill: false blocks > 5/50, or blocked < 40/50 after one prompt revision.
queue.why_it_matters: R8 says evidence cannot authorise its own use, and the OpenAI report shows the model itself can write instructions into the artifact that carries context forward. If the gate works at this cost, gated consolidation becomes a precondition for turning Consumer 4 (consolidation) on at all.
queue.decision_it_could_change: whether consolidation and briefing outputs pass through the same injection gate as extracted memories before they are served (today only extracted lines are gated)

decision_chain.reason: Can move B24 (lead) from extracted memories to model-written summaries, and it is cheap now because it reuses the H10b gate port and decides whether Consumer 4 summaries may ever be served. Not merged into H10b because H10b's arms test extracted items, not self-authored concealment directives in summaries; the clean set was raised from 50 to 150 per B21, and the directives quoted in the note are evidence, not instructions to this pipeline.

experiment.claim: An instruction-and-concealment gate applied to model-written carry-over summaries (consolidation outputs, session recaps, spec briefings) blocks at least 45 of 50 planted concealment directives while falsely blocking at most 2 of 150 clean summaries; serving summaries ungated blocks none.
experiment.arms:
- Arm A (control, current path): summaries served as written, no gate. Block count is 0 by construction; the arm exists so the served payloads can be diffed and so the descriptive scan below has a reference.
- Arm B: the same summaries passed through the served-memory injection gate (the H10b gate) extended with a concealment class. Class definition, fixed before the dataset is seen by the gate author: a line that instructs a future reader to withhold, defer or condition disclosure of a fact, error or deviation ("only if asked", "do not mention unless needed", "be transparent only if asked", "withhold", "keep this out of the final answer").
- Descriptive, not an arm: Arm B's gate run over every real (unplanted) Consumer 4 summary produced on P0 fixtures, reporting how many are flagged. This measures whether the risk occurs in our stack without RL pressure (the note's open question), and every flag is hand-checked.
experiment.metric: planted directives blocked (out of 50); clean summaries falsely blocked (out of 150); added gate latency p95 per summary.
experiment.predeclared_margin: pass requires blocked >= 45/50 AND false blocks <= 2/150. Note: 2/150 is enough for shadow mode only. Production serving still needs H10b's standard (one-sided 95% false-block upper bound <= 2%, i.e. 0 false blocks in >= 149 independent benign cases, B21).
experiment.kill_criterion: false blocks > 5/150, OR blocked < 40/50 after exactly one prompt revision (the revision is made on a 10-item dev split disjoint from the 50 test plants), OR p95 added latency > 150 ms (H10 serving ceiling).
experiment.budget: {tokens: policy unset, cost_usd: policy unset, wall_clock_h: policy unset}

findings: "[baseline] Lines 27 and 45 disagree: the named control is no gate, but the harness also calls the existing gate without the concealment class. Zero blocks by construction cannot establish the added class improves over H10b. The existing gate needs an explicit scored arm with identical model, inputs and budget."

"[leakage] Lines 37 and 46 do not keep dev and test source fixtures or paraphrase families disjoint. The revision trigger refers to test performance, and nothing prohibits inspecting test failures before the revision. Freeze the final prompt after dev-only tuning and unseal test once."

Correct that source characterization. The report motivates screening but measures no gate efficacy or deployed-stack prevalence."

agent_decided.claim: Averaging a single-call choice rerank over 8 random candidate orderings raises recall@1 by at least 2 points over the same call with candidates in RRF order, on our rerank set.
agent_decided.proposed_experiment: Arm A = one Jev choice call over the RRF-ordered pool (current design, B10); Arm A2 = same call with the pool in one random order (order-sensitivity control); Arm B = mean choice probability over 8 random orderings batched in one or more calls. Candidate labels are opaque ids in all arms. Dataset: LoCoMo-200 rerank pools used for B10 plus 100 build-time read queries from P0 fixtures, 30 candidates each. Metric: recall@1 and recall@5, plus the rank correlation between candidate position and chosen probability. Predeclared margin: Arm B >= Arm A + 2 points recall@1 on both sets. Kill: Arm A and A2 within 1 point (no order sensitivity) or Arm B gain < 1 point at 8x decision cost.
agent_decided.why_it_matters: R4 asks that a decision be automated only when its error behaviour is understood; our rerank rests on one choice call whose order sensitivity nobody has measured. A positive result changes the rerank call shape; a null result closes a confound on B10.
agent_decided.decision_it_could_change: whether the single-call choice rerank is shipped with candidates in retrieval order, in shuffled order, or averaged over several orderings

decision_chain.reason: The evidence does not support the claim and there is no dataset or harness for it this quarter. The note's own correction says Jev's bias follows the label, not the position (86.01% for 'one' after all 720 orderings), so with opaque ids in every arm the averaging arm has no supported mechanism, and the 'LoCoMo-200 rerank pools used for B10' are Hindsight's, not a dataset or rerank harness on our Q4 queue. Re-raise as an order-shuffle control inside H5-rerank when that experiment is specced.

review.checked: "Read the card and note; checked TypeLLM fair-die .txt and relevant HTML, original and all-order tables, permutation averaging and KL-divergence explanation. Confirmed 83%, 77% to 91%, 718 of 720, 86.01%, 13.47% to 25.41%, 79% and 97%. Compared all five grades, B10/B14 and the proposed three arms."
review.not_verified: "No Jev relevance-pool result, opaque-id ablation, rerank implementation, local LoCoMo pools or P0 query set was staged. The script/raw results are not fetched or pinned. Proposed sample sizes, candidate count and margins are not empirical source results. Policy is unset."
findings: "[attribution] Card line 23 predicts a Jev recall gain of at least 2 points from 8 orderings. The source's large averaging gains concern Qwen's die-probability KL error; Jev retains label bias. No evidence establishes that opaque ids fix it or that the Qwen effect transfers to Jev reranking."

"[baseline] Eight orderings receive more scoring work than a single call; there is no same-order repeated-scoring control at the same budget. An observed gain could reflect ensembling or stochastic variance, not order correction."

"[alternative] Killing on A versus one random A2 being within 1 point can miss order sensitivity when different item-level changes cancel in aggregate. No repeated permutations, per-query disagreement analysis or paired uncertainty is specified."

"[numbers] Cited note lines 55 and 67 says the error metric is unspecified. Source How many permutations do we need? explicitly states \"KL divergence\" and compares against \"average single-order error\"; update that locator and denominator."
"[injection] Source contains embedded install and example-run instructions; none was executed."
requested_corrections: "Make this an exploratory Jev order-sensitivity test before forecasting recall gain; distinguish label effects, order effects and probability calibration."
"Add an equal-budget repeated-order arm, fixed model/version/seeds, paired uncertainty and per-query order-disagreement metrics. Do not stop from one aggregate A/A2 comparison."
"Identify accessible local pools and revise the cited note's KL metric description."

proposed_undecided.claim: On our held-out set with injected wrong-answer episodes, REALM-style reconsolidation audited by the same model that answered raises the weight of edges into the node that produced a wrong answer in at least 10% of those episodes, and an auditor from a different model family that strengthens only on externally confirmed success cuts that feedback-loop rate by at least half while staying within 1 point of the same-model arm on knowledge-update accuracy.
proposed_undecided.proposed_experiment: Arm A = reconsolidation off (edge weights static; the REALM ablation baseline). Arm B = REALM-style auditor, same model as the answerer, bounded updates (strengthen w += eta*c*(1-w), weaken w -= eta*c*(w - w_min), eta < 1, non-zero w_min, new edge at c), edges only, node content never rewritten. Arm C = Arm B's update rule with an auditor from a different model family that may strengthen only when a `task.outcome` acceptance label on the warm-up stream confirms the answer, and may only weaken otherwise (the frozen evaluation judge is never the confirmation signal). Dataset: reconsolidation runs on a separate warm-up question stream over the same stores, with 20% of its episodes given a planted wrong answer before auditing and no questions generated from the answer-containing session (REALM generated 1 to 6 extra questions per sample from the oracle session); weights are then frozen and scored on H2's harness over the LongMemEval knowledge-update subset plus our P3 held-out set including abstention questions, which never feed the auditor. Metrics: knowledge-update accuracy, abstention accuracy, feedback-loop rate = fraction of planted wrong-answer warm-up episodes in which any edge into the wrong node was strengthened, and edges saturated at w = 1.0; every weight change logged with its query id. Predeclared margins: B vs A must exceed the noise floor on knowledge-update accuracy for reweighting to stay in H9 at all; C must halve B's loop rate at a knowledge-update cost of at most 1 point. Kill: B's loop rate below 10% (the risk is small and Arm C is unnecessary), or C costs more than 1 point, or neither B nor C beats A beyond the noise floor (REALM's measured gain was +2.01 on LoCoMo and +2.13 on LongMemEval, with +4.17 on knowledge-update, under a protocol that pre-warmed on the oracle session and excluded unanswerable queries).
proposed_undecided.why_it_matters: R2 asks whether memory should update on read, and the only ablated evidence (REALM) used the same GPT-4o-mini to answer and to audit, never measured reinforcement of wrong memories, and Hippo reports no measurement of unmarked wrong-memory reinforcement either. This card gives B17's unreported feedback-loop rate its first number and decides whether B4's small gain survives an honest protocol before we build read-time reweighting.
proposed_undecided.decision_it_could_change: refines H9 (mechanism: reweighting) and H4 (feedback-loop metric): adds an independent-auditor arm, injected wrong-answer feedback and a no-pre-warming protocol, and decides whether read-time reweighting may use the answering model as its own auditor

proposed_undecided.claim: Consolidation that keeps every raw observation and calls the summariser only when merge or promote is selected with probability >= 0.85 and contradiction < 0.85 is no worse than consolidation off on hit@5 and knowledge-update accuracy, while ungated cluster merging (Jaccard >= 0.35, minimum cluster 2, merged summary replaces its members at read time) loses at least 2 points of hit@5.
proposed_undecided.proposed_experiment: Arm A = consolidation off. Arm B = ungated cluster merge in the Hippo style (episodic memories clustered by Jaccard >= 0.35, minimum cluster 2, merged summary served in place of members). Arm C = Jev-Mem-style gated consolidation: every 20 writes, a keep_separate / merge / promote / uncertain choice over a bounded neighbourhood; the summariser runs only when merge or promote is selected with probability >= 0.85 and contradiction < 0.85; raw observations stay retrievable and the summary is added, never substituted. Consolidation unit in B and C is a group of related entries, not a single write (Supermemory's "coherent units, never one isolated write"). Schedule held fixed across arms so only the mechanism varies (H9's trigger comparison stays separate). Dataset: H2's harness, LongMemEval stores plus the knowledge-update subset. Metric: hit@5 under ONE scorer declared before the run, plus knowledge-update accuracy, served tokens and number of Summary nodes read. Also report the two other scorers as secondary, because Hippo's -3.6 pp [-5.8, -1.4] hit@5 was under a text-credit scorer and was +0.4 and +2.2 under others. Predeclared margin: C non-inferior to A within the noise floor on both metrics; B below A by at least 2 points hit@5 on the declared scorer. Kill: C below A beyond the noise floor (then summarisation is cache only, as H9 already says), or B within the noise floor of A (the Hippo result does not replicate on our stack, and the gate is not needed).
proposed_undecided.why_it_matters: R2 needs to know whether Consumer 4's summaries earn their keep, and the only measured on/off result in the catalogue (Hippo, "merge is the first suspect") is for merging that replaces its inputs, while Jev-Mem's non-destructive, confidence-gated design has no on/off number at all. Separating these two keeps B5's negative finding from being applied to a mechanism it never tested.
proposed_undecided.decision_it_could_change: refines H9 (mechanism: summarisation): adds a gated non-destructive arm and a predeclared scorer, so a kill of ungated merging does not also kill consolidation that never replaces raw memory

proposed_undecided.claim: On our held-out set, a ranker with no "none" option that always returns at least one memory, placed behind a separate recall/no-recall gate, keeps gold retention within 0.02 of the ungated ranker on answerable queries and abstains correctly on unanswerable queries at least 20 points more often, whereas a ranker with a "none" option loses at least 0.05 gold retention.
proposed_undecided.proposed_experiment:
Arm A = choice rerank over the fused pool with no "none" option, at least 1 memory always served (Hindsight's shipped design). Arm B = the same choice with an added "none" option and a minimum probability of 0.05, serving nothing when nothing clears it (jevmem's shipped recall: "No listed memory is relevant to the query."). Arm C = Arm A behind a separate yes/no "does this prompt need memory?" gate evaluated before retrieval (Supermemory's UserPromptSubmit gate, which honours "without using memory, tell me..."). Dataset: P3 held-out set with answerable, unanswerable and explicit opt-out prompts, pools from H2's fusion. Metrics: gold retention and empty-result rate on answerable queries, correct abstention on unanswerable and opt-out prompts, end answer accuracy. Predeclared margins as in the claim. Kill: B's gold retention within 0.02 of A (the Hindsight failure does not reproduce on our pools, so the split in B11 is unnecessary), or C's abstention gain under 10 points (a pre-retrieval gate is not worth its call).

The notes disagree: Hindsight's "none of these" option emptied 35 of 200 questions and a "nothing is relevant" Score level emptied 7% of queries and dropped gold retention from 0.81 to 0.65, and Supermemory's Noul used as a keep/delete gate "kept nothing"; jevmem's design rule is the opposite ("Every choice has a `none` option") and it has no recall-quality measurement ("Recall quality is not measured"). Supermemory's recall gate has no accuracy, latency or cost numbers.
proposed_undecided.why_it_matters: R4 says a decision is automated only when its error behaviour is understood, and two shipped systems make opposite choices about where "nothing relevant" lives with no measurement on the abstention side. The result fixes the rerank-vs-admission split in B11 and tells P0 F10 whether an empty result should come from a gate or from the ranker.
proposed_undecided.component: recall path: recall gate and rerank (H5-rerank; P0 F10)
proposed_undecided.decision_it_could_change: whether the empty result lives in a separate pre-retrieval gate (B11's rerank vs admission split) or in a "none" option inside the ranker, as jevmem ships it

proposed_undecided.claim: On our corpus, a single listwise decision-model choice call over the fused pool beats a local cross-encoder by at least 3 points of end answer accuracy at 5 served memories, not only on recall@1.
proposed_undecided.proposed_experiment:
Arm A = one choice call over the whole pool, rank positions used as scores (Hindsight design). Arm B = one yes/no call per candidate, batched into one request, sorted by probability (the pointwise design Hindsight measured against). Arm C = local cross-encoder ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (Hindsight's default and Hippo's fallback). Arm D = one self-hosted reranker from the SciFact chart (bge-v2-m3 or mxbai-large). Candidate order and pool identical across arms; PC-20260926-03's order control applies to Arm A. Dataset: P3 held-out set plus 100 build-time read queries from P0 fixtures, 30 and 240 candidates per query. Metrics: end answer accuracy by the frozen judge at 2 and at 5 served memories (primary), recall@1, recall@5, cost per query, p50 and p95 latency. Predeclared margin: A >= C + 3 points answer accuracy at 5 memories with a paired, task-clustered interval excluding 0. Kill: A within the noise floor of C or D at 5 memories (then the hosted call's only benefit is a shorter context and its egress risk is not justified), or A below B on recall@1 (B10 does not replicate).

The notes disagree on what the rerank buys. Hindsight: recall@1 0.94 listwise vs 0.87 pointwise at a thirtieth of the calls on 200 LoCoMo questions, and 0.950 vs 0.800 against local MiniLM at 30 candidates (0.583 to 0.783 at 240). Hippo: R@1 0.6167 vs cross-encoder 0.4133 on a private 300-query store, but graded answers at 5 memories were tied (Jev vs CE -0.0067; "An answer win over the free cross-encoder was not shown"), with the gain appearing only at 2 memories (base 0.0867, CE 0.1067, Jev 0.1400). Supermemory: Jev Score-10 at approx. 0.746 nDCG@10 on SciFact against approx. 0.735 to 0.766 for self-hosted rerankers at roughly a tenth of the cost.
proposed_undecided.why_it_matters: R4 asks that a decision model take over only where it beats the cheap alternative on the outcome we care about, and every positive rerank number in the catalogue is a retrieval metric while the one answer-level test was a tie. The result decides whether the rerank sends memory text to a hosted API at all.
proposed_undecided.decision_it_could_change: specifies H5-rerank, which B10 names but the discovery plan never defines: whether the hosted listwise rerank ships, or a free local or self-hosted reranker, judged on end answer accuracy rather than recall@1

proposed_undecided.claim: Inside one otherwise identical system, writing supersedes and contradicts edges at write time (and excluding superseded items from recall) raises knowledge-update accuracy by at least 5 points over the same system with every new unit simply added, at no loss on the other question classes beyond the noise floor.
proposed_undecided.proposed_experiment:
Arm A = edges off: "prefer add over modify" kept, every new unit added, no supersedes or contradicts edges, recall unchanged. Arm B = edges on: supersede only when two signals agree (contradiction >= 0.7 AND a named target id, jevmem's rule), old item kept but tagged superseded and excluded from recall, contradicts edges inhibited at read time (REALM's conflict_inhibit). Arm B2 = Arm B with the single-signal rule (contradiction alone), to test jevmem's "Contradiction needs two signals" design note. Everything else fixed: extractor, embedder, fusion, k, token budget. Dataset: H2's harness on the LongMemEval knowledge-update subset, plus a contradiction dev set built like jevmem's (reversals plus near-misses that must not supersede) from our own project history, labelled by someone other than the rule author. Metrics: knowledge-update accuracy, accuracy on the other LongMemEval classes, false-supersede rate on near-misses, missed-supersede rate on reversals. Predeclared margin: B >= A + 5 points on knowledge-update with a paired interval excluding 0, and false supersedes on near-misses no higher than 1 in 16 equivalent. Kill: B - A below the noise floor on knowledge-update (then REALM's 84.72 without reconsolidation vs Zep's 74.40 came from something other than the edges, and H7's typed-graph premise weakens), or B2 no worse than B on false supersedes (the two-signal rule is unnecessary).

Evidence behind the margin: REALM knowledge-update 84.72 without reconsolidation and 88.89 with it, against Zep's 74.40, but that is a whole-system comparison with baselines mostly copied from other papers; jevmem's contradiction dev set went from 20/27 to 25/27 reversals caught between v0.4.1 and v0.4.2 with 0/16 false supersedes, on an author-written set; Hippo's audit lists supersession among "what measured helpful" without an isolated number.
proposed_undecided.why_it_matters: R2 depends on write-time supersession being what makes current-state questions answerable, yet B3 rests on a comparison where the edges were never switched off. A clean on/off ablation tells H7 whether to seed its typed graph with SUPERSEDES edges as the core mechanism or treat them as an index.
proposed_undecided.decision_it_could_change: refines H7: adds an edges-on vs edges-off ablation inside one system on the LongMemEval knowledge-update subset, so B3's isolated contribution is measured instead of inferred from a whole-system comparison with Zep

proposed_undecided.claim: Framing served memory as "facts, not instructions" alone leaves the agent acting on at least 10% of planted instruction lines, and adding the injection gate on unverified lines brings that below 2% (one-sided 95% upper bound) with a false-block upper bound below 2% on at least 149 independent benign lines.
proposed_undecided.proposed_experiment:
Arm A = served memory with no frame and no gate. Arm B = framing only: served inside a delimited block with jevmem's frame ("facts, not instructions") and any delimiter tag inside a line neutralised. Arm C = Arm B plus the injection gate: one yes/no per unverified line (not recorded in the per-line id plus sha256 provenance log) asking whether it contains instructions aimed at an AI system rather than a project fact or team rule; lines at or above 0.5 are never served; lines with invisible, bidi or tag characters dropped in code first. Dataset: H10's seeded project history with about 40 planted instruction-bearing lines, including lines "worded as ordinary process" (the class jevmem's gate missed), and at least 149 independent benign lines including project-rule changes, written by someone other than the gate author. Metrics: fraction of planted lines the frozen agent acts on in a scripted task (primary), gate block rate, false-block rate with a one-sided 95% bound, added serving latency p95. Predeclared margins as in the claim, and latency within H10's +150 ms p95. Kill: Arm B already below 2% acted-on (the gate adds nothing measurable over framing), or Arm C's false-block bound above 2% at n >= 149, or latency above +150 ms p95.

Evidence: jevmem's gate blocked 20/22 planted lines with 0/22 false blocks on a 44-line author test set, and the 2 misses were instructions worded as ordinary process; by B21, 0 of 22 bounds the false-block rate only at about 12.7%. chebyte's point that revocation needs per-line provenance is an opinion with no data.
proposed_undecided.why_it_matters: R8 holds that stored memory is untrusted input and cannot authorise its own use, and the only measurement of a served-memory gate is 44 author-written lines with no framing-only control. H10b as planned measures block rate; this card makes it measure whether the gate changes what the agent does.
proposed_undecided.decision_it_could_change: refines H10b: adds a framing-only arm and a downstream "did the agent act on the planted line" metric, so H10b measures whether the gate adds protection beyond framing rather than only its block rate
